programme.title: Amazon ECS and AWS Fargate Follow Along
programme.outcome: Build and push a private ECR image; create an ECS cluster, Fargate task definition and ECS service; integrate the service with an Application Load Balancer; separate task and execution IAM roles; send container logs to CloudWatch; configure ECS Service Auto Scaling and demonstrate controlled scale-out; compare ECS, EKS, Fargate and Lambda; then safely delete only resources created by the lab.
programme.statusNotice: Offline authoring manuscript only — not locally validated, imported, accepted, approved, published or fingerprinted.
programme.administratorAccessModel: Use an existing AWS administrator account for this disposable training lab. Do not create a separate human IAM user or static access key.
completionDefinition: The existing AWS administrator training account is verified and used without creating a separate human IAM user/access key.
A custom Flask application image is built in AWS CloudShell, health-tested locally and pushed to private ECR as immutable tag v1.
A two-AZ VPC, ALB, IP target group and restricted ALB-to-task security-group flow are created.
Separate ECS task execution and application task roles are created; the application proves task-role access by reading one exact SSM parameter.
A Fargate task definition uses awsvpc, 0.25 vCPU/0.5 GB, ECR v1, awslogs and a container /health check.
An ECS service maintains two Fargate tasks across the two subnets and registers healthy task IPs with the ALB.
ECS Service Auto Scaling manages desired count between 2 and 4 using CPU target tracking and a fixed five-minute load test demonstrates scale-out.
The learner can choose ECS, EKS or Lambda based on orchestration/execution requirements and can explain that Fargate is container compute rather than an orchestrator.
All automation, tasks, ALB/ECR/log/IAM/network resources and CloudShell files are removed in reverse dependency order while the existing administrator account remains unchanged.

editableBlocks.title: app.py
Dockerfile
editableBlocks.content:
FROM public.ecr.aws/docker/library/python:3.12-slim

WORKDIR /app

COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

COPY app.py .

EXPOSE 8080

CMD ["gunicorn", "--bind", "0.0.0.0:8080", "--workers", "2", "--threads", "2", "--access-logfile", "-", "--error-logfile", "-", "app:app"]

editableBlocks.title: register-task-definition.sh
generate-load.sh
editableBlocks.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

if [ "$#" -ne 1 ]; then
  echo "Usage: ./generate-load.sh <ALB_DNS_NAME>"
  exit 1
fi

ALB_DNS_NAME="$1"
END_TIME=$((SECONDS + 300))
PIDS=()

for WORKER in 1 2 3 4; do
  (
    while [ "$SECONDS" -lt "$END_TIME" ]; do
      curl --fail --silent --show-error \
        "http://${ALB_DNS_NAME}/burn?seconds=5" \
        >/dev/null || true
    done
  ) &
  PIDS+=("$!")
done

for PID in "${PIDS[@]}"; do
  wait "$PID"
done

echo "Controlled five-minute load test finished."

tasks.title: Create the private Amazon ECR repository
tasks.goal: Create fa-ecs-fargate-eks-app as a private ECR repository with immutable tags and scan-on-push enabled.
tasks.whyItMatters: The registry becomes the controlled image source that the Fargate task execution role pulls from later.
tasks.examRelevance: ECR is the AWS-native private registry commonly paired with ECS task definitions.

browserSteps.instruction: Open Amazon ECR in eu-west-2.
Choose Repositories.
Choose Create repository.
Visibility: Private.
Repository name: fa-ecs-fargate-eks-app.
Image tag mutability: Immutable.
Turn scan on push on.
Create the repository.
Open it and copy/record the repository URI.

cliBlocks.title: CloudShell - create ECR repository
cliBlocks.content: ECR_URI="$(aws ecr create-repository --repository-name fa-ecs-fargate-eks-app --image-tag-mutability IMMUTABLE --image-scanning-configuration scanOnPush=true --query repository.repositoryUri --output text --region eu-west-2)"

expectedResults: The private repository exists in eu-west-2.
Tag mutability is IMMUTABLE.
Scan on push is enabled.

verificationChecks.text: The repository name is exactly fa-ecs-fargate-eks-app.
The generated URI includes the current AWS account ID.

tasks.title: Build, test and push container image v1
tasks.goal: Build the application image in CloudShell, run a local health check, authenticate Docker to ECR and push immutable tag v1.
tasks.whyItMatters: Testing before pushing separates application-image faults from later ECS networking or IAM faults.
tasks.examRelevance: Fargate pulls the image specified in the task definition; ECR authorization is handled through the task execution role at runtime.

browserSteps.instruction: Remain in ~/fa-ecs-fargate-eks.
Build the image as fa-ecs-fargate-eks-app:v1.
Run the image locally mapping local TCP 8080 to container TCP 8080.
Use curl against http://localhost:8080/health and confirm healthy.
Stop/remove the local test container.
Get the account ID and ECR registry URI.

Authenticate Docker to ECR with aws ecr get-login-password piped to docker login --password-stdin. The pipe intentionally sends the short-lived ECR authorization password to Docker through standard input rather than putting it in a file.
Tag the image with the exact private ECR URI and v1.
Push v1.
Open ECR and confirm image tag v1 appears.

cliBlocks.title: CloudShell - authenticate Docker
cliBlocks.content: aws ecr get-login-password --region eu-west-2 | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin "$ECR_REGISTRY"

cliBlocks.title: CloudShell - verify ECR image
cliBlocks.content: aws ecr describe-images --repository-name fa-ecs-fargate-eks-app --image-ids imageTag=v1 --region eu-west-2

The image push completes successfully.

verificationChecks.text: The ECR image URI ends /fa-ecs-fargate-eks-app:v1.

tasks.title: Create the two-AZ public VPC for ALB and Fargate
tasks.goal: Create fa-ecs-fargate-eks-vpc with one public subnet in eu-west-2a and one in eu-west-2b, an internet gateway and public route table.
tasks.whyItMatters: This cost-conscious lab gives Fargate tasks public IPs so they can pull from ECR and reach CloudWatch/SSM without a NAT gateway; task SG rules still prevent direct inbound application traffic.
tasks.examRelevance: Fargate uses awsvpc networking, so each task receives its own ENI and security groups.

browserSteps.instruction: Open VPC in eu-west-2.
Create VPC fa-ecs-fargate-eks-vpc with CIDR 10.140.0.0/16.
Create fa-ecs-fargate-eks-public-a in eu-west-2a with CIDR 10.140.1.0/24.
Create fa-ecs-fargate-eks-public-b in eu-west-2b with CIDR 10.140.2.0/24.
Enable auto-assign public IPv4 on both subnets.
Create fa-ecs-fargate-eks-igw and attach it to the VPC.
Create fa-ecs-fargate-eks-public-rt.
Add 0.0.0.0/0 -> fa-ecs-fargate-eks-igw.
Associate both public subnets with the route table.
Record the design trade-off: public IPs remove NAT-gateway cost for this lab; production services commonly place tasks in private subnets and provide egress through NAT or private VPC endpoints.

cliBlocks.title: CloudShell - create VPC
cliBlocks.content: VPC_ID="$(aws ec2 create-vpc --cidr-block 10.140.0.0/16 --tag-specifications "ResourceType=vpc,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-ecs-fargate-eks-vpc},{Key=FollowAlong,Value=fa-ecs-fargate-eks}]" --query Vpc.VpcId --output text --region eu-west-2)"

cliBlocks.title: CloudShell - subnet A
cliBlocks.content: SUBNET_A_ID="$(aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id "$VPC_ID" --availability-zone eu-west-2a --cidr-block 10.140.1.0/24 --tag-specifications "ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-ecs-fargate-eks-public-a}]" --query Subnet.SubnetId --output text --region eu-west-2)"

cliBlocks.title: CloudShell - subnet B
cliBlocks.content: SUBNET_B_ID="$(aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id "$VPC_ID" --availability-zone eu-west-2b --cidr-block 10.140.2.0/24 --tag-specifications "ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-ecs-fargate-eks-public-b}]" --query Subnet.SubnetId --output text --region eu-west-2)"

cliBlocks.title: CloudShell - create IGW
cliBlocks.content: IGW_ID="$(aws ec2 create-internet-gateway --tag-specifications "ResourceType=internet-gateway,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-ecs-fargate-eks-igw}]" --query InternetGateway.InternetGatewayId --output text --region eu-west-2)"

cliBlocks.title: CloudShell - create route table
cliBlocks.content: RT_ID="$(aws ec2 create-route-table --vpc-id "$VPC_ID" --tag-specifications "ResourceType=route-table,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-ecs-fargate-eks-public-rt}]" --query RouteTable.RouteTableId --output text --region eu-west-2)"

expectedResults: The VPC spans eu-west-2a and eu-west-2b.
Both subnets route 0.0.0.0/0 to the IGW and auto-assign public IPv4.

verificationChecks.text: The VPC CIDR is 10.140.0.0/16.
No NAT gateway is created.

tasks.title: Create ALB/task security groups, IP target group and Application Load Balancer
tasks.goal: Expose only the ALB on HTTP:80 and allow Fargate task TCP:8080 only from the ALB security group; create an IP target group and listener.
tasks.whyItMatters: Fargate tasks use awsvpc ENIs, so an ECS/ALB target group for the service must use IP targets rather than instance targets.
tasks.examRelevance: The ALB creates a stable client endpoint while ECS registers/deregisters task IPs as the service changes.
warnings: The ALB is chargeable while running. Complete the lab and cleanup promptly.

browserSteps.instruction: Open EC2 > Security Groups.
Create fa-ecs-fargate-eks-alb-sg in the training VPC.
Allow inbound HTTP TCP 80 from 0.0.0.0/0; keep default outbound.
Create fa-ecs-fargate-eks-task-sg.
Allow inbound Custom TCP 8080 from fa-ecs-fargate-eks-alb-sg only.
Do not allow TCP 8080 from the internet.
Open Target Groups and create fa-ecs-fargate-eks-tg.
Target type: IP addresses.
Protocol/port: HTTP:8080.
VPC: fa-ecs-fargate-eks-vpc.
Health check path: /health; success code 200.
Do not manually register targets.
Create internet-facing Application Load Balancer fa-ecs-fargate-eks-alb across both training public subnets using fa-ecs-fargate-eks-alb-sg.
Create HTTP:80 listener forwarding to fa-ecs-fargate-eks-tg.
Wait for the ALB to become Active and record its DNS name.

cliBlocks.title: CloudShell - rebuild network IDs
cliBlocks.content: VPC_ID="$(aws ec2 describe-vpcs --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=fa-ecs-fargate-eks-vpc --query "Vpcs[0].VpcId" --output text --region eu-west-2)"; SUBNET_A_ID="$(aws ec2 describe-subnets --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=fa-ecs-fargate-eks-public-a --query "Subnets[0].SubnetId" --output text --region eu-west-2)"; SUBNET_B_ID="$(aws ec2 describe-subnets --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=fa-ecs-fargate-eks-public-b --query "Subnets[0].SubnetId" --output text --region eu-west-2)"

cliBlocks.title: CloudShell - create ALB SG
cliBlocks.content: ALB_SG_ID="$(aws ec2 create-security-group --group-name fa-ecs-fargate-eks-alb-sg --description "HTTP to ECS training ALB" --vpc-id "$VPC_ID" --tag-specifications "ResourceType=security-group,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-ecs-fargate-eks-alb-sg}]" --query GroupId --output text --region eu-west-2)"

cliBlocks.title: CloudShell - create task SG
cliBlocks.content: TASK_SG_ID="$(aws ec2 create-security-group --group-name fa-ecs-fargate-eks-task-sg --description "Application traffic only from ALB" --vpc-id "$VPC_ID" --tag-specifications "ResourceType=security-group,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-ecs-fargate-eks-task-sg}]" --query GroupId --output text --region eu-west-2)"

cliBlocks.title: CloudShell - create IP target group
cliBlocks.content: TG_ARN="$(aws elbv2 create-target-group --name fa-ecs-fargate-eks-tg --protocol HTTP --port 8080 --target-type ip --vpc-id "$VPC_ID" --health-check-path /health --health-check-protocol HTTP --matcher HttpCode=200 --tags Key=FollowAlong,Value=fa-ecs-fargate-eks --query "TargetGroups[0].TargetGroupArn" --output text --region eu-west-2)"

cliBlocks.title: CloudShell - create ALB
cliBlocks.content: ALB_ARN="$(aws elbv2 create-load-balancer --name fa-ecs-fargate-eks-alb --scheme internet-facing --type application --ip-address-type ipv4 --subnets "$SUBNET_A_ID" "$SUBNET_B_ID" --security-groups "$ALB_SG_ID" --tags Key=FollowAlong,Value=fa-ecs-fargate-eks --query "LoadBalancers[0].LoadBalancerArn" --output text --region eu-west-2)"

cliBlocks.title: CloudShell - create listener
cliBlocks.content: LISTENER_ARN="$(aws elbv2 create-listener --load-balancer-arn "$ALB_ARN" --protocol HTTP --port 80 --default-actions Type=forward,TargetGroupArn="$TG_ARN" --query "Listeners[0].ListenerArn" --output text --region eu-west-2)"

cliBlocks.title: CloudShell - get DNS
cliBlocks.content: ALB_DNS="$(aws elbv2 describe-load-balancers --load-balancer-arns "$ALB_ARN" --query "LoadBalancers[0].DNSName" --output text --region eu-west-2)"; printf "ALB_DNS=%s\n" "$ALB_DNS"

expectedResults: The ALB is Active across both AZs.
The target group type is ip.
Task SG port 8080 accepts traffic only from the ALB SG.

verificationChecks.text: The listener forwards HTTP:80 to fa-ecs-fargate-eks-tg.
No task target is registered yet.

tasks.title: Create ECS execution/task IAM roles, CloudWatch log group and training parameter
tasks.goal: Create separate execution and task roles, create the awslogs destination, and create the exact SSM parameter the application reads.
tasks.whyItMatters: The execution role is used by ECS/Fargate infrastructure to pull ECR images and send logs; the task role is delivered to application containers for AWS API calls.
tasks.examRelevance: Confusing execution-role permissions with application task-role permissions is a common container-security design mistake.

browserSteps.instruction: Open IAM > Roles > Create role.
Create fa-ecs-fargate-eks-execution-role trusted by ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com.
Attach AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy.
Create fa-ecs-fargate-eks-task-role with the same ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com trust principal.
Add inline policy fa-ecs-fargate-eks-task-ssm allowing only ssm:GetParameter on /fa-ecs-fargate-eks/message in this account and eu-west-2.
Open CloudWatch > Log groups and create /ecs/fa-ecs-fargate-eks.
Set retention to 1 day.
Open Systems Manager > Parameter Store.
Create String parameter /fa-ecs-fargate-eks/message with value hello-from-task-iam-role.
Do not give the task role ECR or CloudWatch Logs permissions; those belong to the execution role in this design.

cliBlocks.title: CloudShell - derive account and write task policy
cliBlocks.content: AWS_ACCOUNT_ID="$(aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text)"; sed "s/ACCOUNT_ID/${AWS_ACCOUNT_ID}/g" task-ssm-policy.template.json > task-ssm-policy.json

cliBlocks.title: CloudShell - attach task inline policy
cliBlocks.content: aws iam put-role-policy --role-name fa-ecs-fargate-eks-task-role --policy-name fa-ecs-fargate-eks-task-ssm --policy-document file://task-ssm-policy.json

cliBlocks.title: CloudShell - create SSM parameter
cliBlocks.content: aws ssm put-parameter --name /fa-ecs-fargate-eks/message --type String --value hello-from-task-iam-role --region eu-west-2

expectedResults: Both IAM roles exist.
The execution role has AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy.
The task role can read only the training SSM parameter.
The log group and parameter exist.

verificationChecks.text: The two role ARNs are different.
The log retention is 1 day.

tasks.title: Create the ECS cluster and register the Fargate task definition
tasks.goal: Create the ECS cluster and register a Fargate task definition using the ECR image, awsvpc, two IAM roles, awslogs and container health check.
tasks.whyItMatters: The task definition is the versioned application blueprint while the cluster is the logical ECS orchestration boundary.
tasks.examRelevance: Fargate task definitions require awsvpc networking and supported CPU/memory combinations.

browserSteps.instruction: Open Amazon ECS.
Choose Clusters > Create cluster.
Cluster name: fa-ecs-fargate-eks-cluster.
Create the cluster without adding EC2 container instances.
In CloudShell run register-task-definition.sh.
Open ECS > Task definitions > fa-ecs-fargate-eks-task.
Open revision 1.
Confirm launch compatibility includes Fargate.
Confirm CPU 0.25 vCPU and memory 0.5 GB.
Confirm network mode awsvpc.
Confirm execution role and task role are different.
Confirm container port 8080, awslogs configuration and /health container health check.

cliBlocks.title: CloudShell - create cluster
cliBlocks.content: aws ecs create-cluster --cluster-name fa-ecs-fargate-eks-cluster --tags key=FollowAlong,value=fa-ecs-fargate-eks --region eu-west-2

cliBlocks.title: CloudShell - capture task definition ARN

editableBlocks.title: register-task-definition.sh

expectedResults: The ECS cluster is Active.

executionRoleArn and taskRoleArn are both set.

tasks.title: Create the two-task Fargate ECS service behind the ALB
tasks.goal: Create fa-ecs-fargate-eks-service with desired count 2 across both public subnets, public task ENIs, task SG and ALB target group.
tasks.whyItMatters: An ECS service continuously maintains the desired number of tasks and integrates task registration with the load balancer.
tasks.examRelevance: Fargate removes EC2 container-host management while ECS remains the orchestrator.
warnings: Fargate tasks, task public IPv4 addresses and the ALB are chargeable while running. Complete verification/scaling and cleanup promptly.

browserSteps.instruction: Open ECS > fa-ecs-fargate-eks-cluster > Services > Create.
Compute options: Launch type.
Launch type: FARGATE.
Platform version: LATEST.
Application type: Service.
Task definition family: fa-ecs-fargate-eks-task, latest revision.
Service name: fa-ecs-fargate-eks-service.
Desired tasks: 2.
VPC: fa-ecs-fargate-eks-vpc.
Subnets: both training public subnets.
Security group: fa-ecs-fargate-eks-task-sg.
Public IP: Turned on for this lab.
Load balancing: Application Load Balancer.
Use existing fa-ecs-fargate-eks-alb listener and fa-ecs-fargate-eks-tg.
Container: fa-ecs-fargate-eks-app:8080.
Health check grace period: 60 seconds.
Create the service.
Wait until the service reports 2 Running tasks and the target group reports 2 healthy IP targets.

cliBlocks.title: CloudShell - rebuild service networking

editableBlocks.title: generate-load.sh
editableBlocks.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

if [ "$#" -ne 1 ]; then
  echo "Usage: ./generate-load.sh <ALB_DNS_NAME>"
  exit 1
fi

ALB_DNS_NAME="$1"
END_TIME=$((SECONDS + 300))
PIDS=()

for WORKER in 1 2 3 4; do
  (
    while [ "$SECONDS" -lt "$END_TIME" ]; do
      curl --fail --silent --show-error \
        "http://${ALB_DNS_NAME}/burn?seconds=5" \
        >/dev/null || true
    done
  ) &
  PIDS+=("$!")
done

for PID in "${PIDS[@]}"; do
  wait "$PID"
done

echo "Controlled five-minute load test finished."

expectedResults: CPU rises during controlled /burn traffic.
The service can increase desired count above 2, up to maximum 4.
New Fargate tasks are automatically registered with the ALB target group.

verificationChecks.text: Desired count never exceeds 4.
The application remains reachable through the ALB during scale-out.

tasks.title: Compare ECS, EKS, Fargate and Lambda

tasks.whyItMatters: A correct SAA-C03 answer usually starts with execution/orchestration requirements, not familiarity with a service name.
tasks.examRelevance: ECS and EKS orchestrate containers; Lambda is a serverless function execution model; Fargate supplies serverless container compute for supported orchestration platforms.

browserSteps.instruction: Open service-selection.json.

Apply the exam rule: AWS-native container service with no Kubernetes requirement -> ECS; Kubernetes requirement -> EKS; event-driven function -> Lambda.
Relate the live lab to the decision: this is ECS orchestration + Fargate compute + ECR registry + ALB + Application Auto Scaling + CloudWatch.

Exam trigger: no Kubernetes requirement + containers -> ECS is often simpler.
Exam trigger: Kubernetes API/ecosystem requirement -> EKS.
Exam trigger: event-driven function execution -> Lambda.
Exam trigger: serverless containers without managing EC2 hosts -> Fargate as the compute option.

troubleshooting.title: Docker build fails in CloudShell
troubleshooting.likelyCause: Docker engine is not ready, the Dockerfile/app files are incomplete, or a package download failed.
troubleshooting.fix: Run docker info, confirm all files exist in ~/fa-ecs-fargate-eks, rerun python3 -m py_compile app.py, then rebuild.

troubleshooting.title: ECR push says no basic auth credentials
troubleshooting.likelyCause: Docker has not authenticated to the account's eu-west-2 ECR registry or the login token expired.
troubleshooting.fix: Rebuild ECR_REGISTRY from get-caller-identity and rerun get-login-password piped to docker login before pushing.

troubleshooting.title: Fargate task stops with CannotPullContainerError
troubleshooting.likelyCause: Task public IP/route is missing or the execution role/ECR image URI is wrong.
troubleshooting.fix: Verify assignPublicIp=ENABLED, both subnets route 0.0.0.0/0 to the IGW, v1 exists in ECR, and the execution role has AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy.

troubleshooting.title: Target group health stays unhealthy
troubleshooting.likelyCause: The task SG doesn't permit ALB SG -> TCP 8080, the app failed to start, or /health is not returning 200.
troubleshooting.fix: Inspect ECS service events and CloudWatch logs, verify the task SG source is fa-ecs-fargate-eks-alb-sg and target-group health path is /health.

troubleshooting.title: /config returns AccessDenied
troubleshooting.likelyCause: The task definition uses the wrong task role or its inline SSM policy does not contain the current account ID.
troubleshooting.fix: Describe the task definition, verify taskRoleArn is fa-ecs-fargate-eks-task-role, and inspect fa-ecs-fargate-eks-task-ssm.

troubleshooting.title: No container logs appear
troubleshooting.likelyCause: The awslogs configuration/log group or execution-role permissions are wrong.
troubleshooting.fix: Verify log group /ecs/fa-ecs-fargate-eks exists, the task definition uses awslogs, and the execution role has AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy.

troubleshooting.title: Service Auto Scaling does not scale out
troubleshooting.likelyCause: CPU has not remained above the target long enough, the load script stopped early, or the scalable target/policy is misconfigured.
troubleshooting.fix: Verify min=2/max=4, target=30, run the fixed five-minute four-worker load once, and review ECS service events/CloudWatch CPU before changing the policy.

troubleshooting.title: Target group deletion fails during cleanup
troubleshooting.likelyCause: The ALB listener or ECS service still references the target group.
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm the ECS service is deleted, delete the listener and ALB, then retry the exact target group.

troubleshooting.title: Security group or subnet deletion fails
troubleshooting.likelyCause: ALB or Fargate ENIs have not been released yet.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait after ALB/service deletion, verify no fa-ecs-fargate-eks ENI remains in the VPC, then retry only the exact lab resource.

warnings.cost: This lab creates an Application Load Balancer, at least two AWS Fargate tasks and public IPv4 addresses for the tasks, plus ECR and CloudWatch Logs usage. These can incur charges. The public-subnet task design intentionally avoids a NAT gateway for training cost control.
warnings.safety: Use only the existing disposable AWS administrator training account and exact fa-ecs-fargate-eks resource names/derived IDs. Do not run the controlled CPU generator for more than its fixed five minutes, and never delete unrelated account roles, service-linked roles, networks or repositories.
warnings.credentials: This Follow Along creates no separate human IAM user or static access key. CloudShell uses the current administrator session.
